blocks.content: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is the central bank of India. It regulates the country's monetary system and manages the currency and credit system of the economy. It plays a vital role in maintaining financial stability and controlling inflation.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) was established on April 1, 1935, based on the recommendations of the Hilton Young Commission (Royal Commission on Indian Currency and Finance).
RBI was nationalised on January 1, 1949, transforming it into a fully government-owned central banking institution.
Acts as the issuer of currency notes (excluding ₹1 notes and coins, which are issued by the Ministry of Finance) and sole banker to the Central and State Governments.
Manages country's monetary policy through quantitative instruments (Repo, Reverse Repo, CRR, SLR, OMO) and qualitative instruments (Moral Suasion, Margin Requirements).
Serves as the 'Lender of Last Resort' for commercial banks and regulates the country's foreign exchange under the Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA), 1999.

blocks.content: • It was established under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
• The headquarters of RBI is located in Mumbai.
• To regulate the issue of banknotes.
• To maintain monetary stability in the country.
• To operate the currency and credit system.
The Reserve Bank of India is the supreme monetary authority of the nation, acting as the banker to the government and custodian of foreign exchange reserves.

cells: RBI issues currency notes except one-rupee note.
RBI manages accounts of central and state governments.

blocks.content: • Repo Rate – Rate at which RBI lends money to commercial banks.
• Reverse Repo Rate – Rate at which RBI borrows money from banks.
• Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) – Percentage of deposits banks must keep with RBI.
• Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) – Percentage of deposits banks must maintain in liquid assets.

rows: Control total volume and quantity of credit in the entire economy
Regulate the channel, direction, and specific allocation of credit
General, indirect, and affects all sectors uniformly

blocks.content: • Open Market Operations – Buying and selling government securities.
• Central Board of Directors – Governing body.

items: Hilton Young Commission (1926) recommended the creation of the Reserve Bank of India.
Re-1 note bears the signature of the Finance Secretary, while all other bank notes carry the signature of the RBI Governor.
Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) is maintained in cash form with the RBI, whereas Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) is maintained by commercial banks with themselves in liquid assets.
Osborne Smith was the first Governor of RBI, while C.D. Deshmukh was the first Indian Governor.
